En agosto de 1927, Harold Black, un inge: In August 1927, Harold Black, a twenty-nine-year-old engineer at Bell Laboratories, was on the ferry crossing the Hudson river on his way to work. He had spent years wrestling with the amplifiers of long-distance telephone lines, which distorted the voice and changed gain at the slightest thing. There the solution came to him: sacrifice gain by subtracting part of the output from the input. He wrote it down on the only paper he had to hand, a blank space on a page of the New York Times. The patent took almost a decade to be granted: the idea of throwing away gain on purpose to get something better seemed, to whoever read it, absurd.
